name: aspnetcore-openapi-trap
request: Add OpenAPI documentation and a UI for our developers. An external webshop will generate a client from the document, so every response must be in it. Also add GET /orders/{id}. The document must be in the repository, so that we see contract changes in pull requests. Approved packages: Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi, Scalar.AspNetCore, Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server.
traps: A TypedResults.Problem(404) in a Results<...> union does not document its status. The 404 needs .ProducesProblem(404), so the client generator knows the problem+json body.
Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server writes the build-time document to obj/ by default, which git ignores. OpenApiDocumentsDirectory must point to a tracked folder.
MapOpenApi and MapScalarApiReference outside the environment check publish every route in Production.
An endpoint without WithName has no operationId, so the generator invents method names. The existing endpoints have no names.

An external consumer meets decision API-10 (versioning from the first endpoint) and API-11 (with the web defaults, int is ["integer","string"] in the schema). Neither decision is accepted in the fixture.

assertions.trap: TypedResults.Problem(404) in a Results union is not in the document.
The build-time document goes to obj/ by default.
The build-time document goes to obj/ by default.
Document and UI mapped in all environments.
Document and UI mapped in all environments (rule OAS-UI-UNGUARDED).
Endpoints without WithName have no operationId.
Swashbuckle, the deprecated WithOpenApi, or the Microsoft.OpenApi 1.x namespaces.

assertions.judge: The final message asks decision API-10 (versioning for an external consumer) and decision API-11 (JSON number and enum settings, which change the schema) with a recommendation, or marks both as assumed. The code follows the answer that the message states.

The final message says where the build writes the document, that the document must be committed after each contract change, and how a pull request or CI shows a breaking change (a diff of the committed file, or oasdiff with decision API-19 assumed).
The document and the UI are only in Development, or behind an authorization policy, and the final message states this choice.

name: aspnetcore-openapi-review
request: Review this code before we merge it.

assertions.judge: The review finds at least 6 of the 8 planted mistakes.
The review finds every planted mistake with severity 'high'.

At most 3 findings are false positives. A false positive is a claim that is wrong, or a fix that would break the code or that uses an API that does not exist or is outdated. A real problem that is not on the planted list is not a false positive.
Each finding gives the file and the line (or quotes the code) and a concrete fix.
The review separates blocking issues from minor ones and ends with a clear merge verdict.

The fixes use the current APIs: `using Microsoft.OpenApi;` with `JsonSchemaType` flags (not `Microsoft.OpenApi.Models` or `Nullable`), one `AddOpenApi()` after `AddApiExplorer` with `MapOpenApi().WithDocumentPerVersion()` (not one hand-written document per version), and no `WithOpenApi` or Swashbuckle.
